skill.name: browser-use
skill.description: Guides browser-use CLI workflows for navigating pages, inspecting state, interacting with elements, capturing screenshots, and extracting web data.
skill.summary: Automate browser sessions with browser-use for web testing, form workflows, screenshots, and data extraction.
skill.author: browser-use

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, command examples, placeholders, and documentation URLs. Confirmed risks involve browser profile copying and cookie files, with additional contextual risk from cloud cookie sync, public tunnels, and browser automation code execution. No prompt injection language was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Browser profile and cookie sync can expose authenticated sessions.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before profile use, default to domain-specific sync, and avoid full profile sync unless the user specifically requests it.

remediation.issue: Cookie export examples use a shared temporary path.
remediation.suggestion: Use a private temporary directory or secure file permissions, then delete exported cookie files immediately after import.

remediation.issue: Local server tunnels can expose private development services.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before starting a tunnel, describe the public exposure, and stop tunnels after the browser review is complete.

remediation.issue: JavaScript and Python execution can operate inside authenticated browser sessions.
remediation.suggestion: Run only trusted snippets and scripts, avoid unreviewed files, and keep code execution away from sensitive accounts unless required.

semantic_findings.title: Authenticated Profile and Cookie Transfer Risk
semantic_findings.description: The skill describes copying local Chrome profiles and syncing cookies to cloud browser profiles, including an option that syncs all cookies. This can expose session tokens and authenticated account access if used without explicit, narrow consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly discuss synced cookies, full profile sync, and cookie export/import. The file also includes consent guardrails, so the risk is controlled but real.

semantic_findings.title: Local Service Exposure Through Public Tunnel
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users to expose a local development server through a Cloudflare tunnel so a cloud browser can reach it. This may publish private local applications if the user does not understand the exposure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The tunnel workflow and persistence note are explicit. The risk depends on what local service is exposed and whether the user approved it.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary Browser Automation Code Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents browser-use eval for JavaScript and browser-use python, including execution from a Python file. Running untrusted code in an authenticated browser session can read page data or manipulate user accounts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented commands directly execute JavaScript and Python in the automation context. The capability is legitimate, but unsafe with untrusted scripts or sensitive sessions.

content.value_statement: Browser tasks often require repeated navigation, state checks, form entry, and screenshots. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through browser-use CLI commands for controlled web automation.
actual_capabilities: Opens pages and maintains browser sessions across commands.
Inspects page state and lists clickable elements with indices.
Clicks, types, selects options, sends keys, and scrolls pages.
Captures screenshots and extracts page titles, text, HTML, values, attributes, and bounding boxes.
Manages Chromium, local Chrome, cloud browser, task, tunnel, and profile workflows.
Supports authenticated browsing flows with explicit profile and cookie handling steps.
limitations: Requires the browser-use CLI and its browser dependencies to be installed and configured.
Browser access, profiles, and cookies depend on the user environment and permissions.
Cloud profiles, tunnels, and cookie sync can expose sensitive data without careful confirmation.
It does not bypass site access controls, rate limits, or terms of service.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-use to open this page: [url]. Inspect the page state and summarize the main clickable elements.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a Form Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate interaction with form fields and verification.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-use to open [url], fill the visible form with this test data: [data], submit it, and capture the final page state.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Evidence for a Bug
prompt_templates.scenario: Debugging a page interaction with screenshots.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-use to reproduce this browser issue: [steps]. Capture screenshots before and after the interaction, then summarize what changed.

prompt_templates.title: Run an Authenticated Remote Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with profile selection and cloud session safeguards.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-use for an authenticated workflow on [site]. Ask before using any profile, restrict the domain, avoid full cookie sync, and close sessions when done.

output_examples.input: Check whether the pricing page loads and whether the signup button is visible.
output: Opened the pricing page in a browser session.
Found the signup button among the clickable elements.
Captured a screenshot for visual review.

output_examples.input: Extract the headline and visible navigation labels from a product page.
output: Read the page title and main headline.
Reported the source URL and noted any missing expected labels.

output_examples.input: Review a local app through a temporary tunnel from a cloud browser.
output: Confirmed the tunnel URL before opening it remotely.
Checked the main page state and captured a screenshot.
Stopped the cloud session and tunnel after the review.

best_practices: Run page state before clicking so element indices are current.
Ask for explicit consent before using profiles, cookies, cloud browsers, or tunnels.
Close browser sessions, remote tasks, and tunnels after each workflow.
anti_patterns: Syncing a full browser profile when a domain-specific profile is enough.
Running untrusted JavaScript or Python inside an authenticated browser session.
Leaving cloud sessions or local tunnels running after the task is complete.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates browser navigation, page inspection, element interaction, screenshots, and web data extraction through the browser-use CLI.

faq.question: Does it require browser-use to be installed?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill assumes the browser-use CLI is installed and configured before commands are used.

faq.question: Can it use my logged-in browser profile?
faq.answer: Yes, but it should ask first because browser profiles can contain cookies, logins, and extensions.

faq.question: Can it run in a cloud browser?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents remote browser sessions, remote tasks, cloud profiles, and proxy options.

faq.question: Can it test local development servers?
faq.answer: Yes. It can open local pages directly or expose a local server through a tunnel for cloud browser access.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive accounts?
faq.answer: Use caution. Confirm profile use, avoid full cookie sync, restrict domains, and close sessions after the task.
